rationale: Eleven of twelve blocking findings are resolved on current source: startup side-effect gating moved to src/cli/startup.ts with a regression test, PlannedAction relocated to layer-neutral @/types/dry-run.js, ACP describe overrides, install try/catch, profile path.join and the would-sign-in status decision, proxy end-caps and non-mutating credential check, setup credential prompts, --dry-run=true/1 parsing, and planner negative-assertion tests. CR-012 (dry-run analytics suppression) remains unresolved — its source file was not touched and no CLI --dry-run analytics gate or per-command statement was added.

findings.title: Startup side-effect gating lacks regression tests
findings.problem: The !isDryRun guards around MigrationRunner, the update check, and the upgrade-notice marker in bin/codemie.js are what keep a dry run from writing, but no test loads this startup path with --dry-run to assert those helpers are not invoked.
findings.impact: Dropping a guard — or isDryRunInvocation mis-slicing argv — would let a dry run execute pending migrations or reach the network and write the seen-version marker with nothing failing.
findings.recommendation: Add a bin/codemie.js dry-run startup test asserting MigrationRunner.runPending, the update check, and the upgrade-notice write are skipped.
findings.check_notes: gating moved to src/cli/startup.ts; startup.test.ts asserts migrations/update-check/upgrade-notice skipped for --dry-run

fix.change: Extracted the three gated startup side effects into src/cli/startup.ts runStartupSideEffects(); bin/codemie.js now calls it, so the guards are unit-testable
fix.test: src/cli/startup.test.ts — npx vitest run --project unit src/cli/startup.test.ts

findings.title: Core type modules import a CLI-command type
findings.problem: PlannedAction, a CLI-output shape, lives in @/cli/commands/shared/dry-run.js and is now imported (type-only) by agents/providers/frameworks core types and base adapters, reversing the documented CLI -> Registry -> Plugin dependency direction.
findings.impact: Type-only, so no runtime cycle, but the core layers are now coupled to a CLI module; relocating or renaming the type touches every core module, and the seam invites future runtime imports down the same path.
findings.recommendation: Move PlannedAction to a layer-neutral shared types module (e.g. under agents/core or a common types dir) and re-point all imports.
findings.check_notes: PlannedAction relocated to layer-neutral @/types/dry-run.js across core types

fix.change: Moved PlanKind/PlannedAction to layer-neutral src/types/dry-run.ts; src/cli/.../dry-run.ts re-exports; re-pointed all agents/providers/frameworks imports off @/cli
fix.test: npx tsc --noEmit (type-only move, resolved via typecheck + describe contract tests)

findings.title: ACP installs preview the plain agent's installer
findings.problem: ClaudeAcpPlugin and CodexAcpPlugin override install() to npm-only but inherit ClaudePlugin/CodexPlugin describeInstall()/describeUninstall(), so a dry run of install claude-acp/codex-acp names the plain native installer and npm package instead of the @agentclientprotocol ACP package.
findings.impact: The install --dry-run preview for ACP variants is wrong (a first-delivery command), telling users an action the npm-only ACP install never performs.
findings.recommendation: Override describeInstall()/describeUninstall() in the ACP plugins to describe their own npm-only package/action.
findings.check_notes: ACP plugins override describeInstall/describeUninstall to name the @agentclientprotocol package

fix.change: Added npm-only describeInstall/describeUninstall overrides to ClaudeAcpPlugin and CodexAcpPlugin naming @agentclientprotocol packages

findings.title: Dry-run previews run outside try/catch
findings.problem: install/uninstall/docs call buildPreviewPlan*/describeInstall() before their try block, so a throw from a describe implementation (e.g. platform/package resolution) becomes an unhandled rejection with no error message or end-cap.
findings.impact: On such a failure the command crashes without the AC8 'nothing was changed' statement or a clean error status.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the dry-run preview calls in the same try/catch (or a dedicated one) that prints the failure and printEndCap with a non-zero exit code.
findings.check_notes: install dry-run branch moved inside try/catch; throwing describe prints failure end-cap

fix.change: Moved install/uninstall dry-run preview calls inside their try block and wrapped docs install dry-run in its own try/catch printing failure end-cap + exit 1

findings.title: Switch/delete previews can name the wrong config file
findings.problem: resolveProfileConfigPath builds the local target by string concatenation and switch/delete previews choose local-vs-global from ConfigLoader.hasLocalConfig while the real switchProfile/deleteProfile resolve the write target themselves; the preview can therefore name a config file the mutation will not touch.
findings.impact: Users see a 'would modify <path>' plan pointing at the wrong config file. (Reachability of the divergence from the real write target was not fully confirmed.)
findings.recommendation: Resolve the preview target from the same path logic the real switch/delete uses, and join segments with path.join.

fix.change: resolveProfileConfigPath now joins the local path with path.join(workingDir,'.codemie','codemie-cli.config.json') matching ConfigLoader.LOCAL_CONFIG

findings.title: Profile status contradicts its read-only tier
findings.problem: profile status is registered tier 2 ('does not modify anything'), whose wrapper prints 'Nothing to preview', but on invalid auth handleStatus(dryRun) also prints a 'would re-authenticate' plan; the real path re-authenticates, i.e. writes credentials.
findings.impact: One invocation emits two contradictory footers, and tier-2's 'does not modify anything' is false for a command that can re-auth. AC5 (status does not re-authenticate) and AC7 (status re-auth describes) conflict, so the intended behavior needs a decision.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether profile status is strictly read-only (suppress the re-auth plan under tier 2) or a would-sign-in describe command (stop printing the read-only footer), then reconcile AC5/AC7.
findings.check_notes: decision B applied: status is tier-1 would-sign-in describe, no read-only footer

fix.change: Option B: re-tiered profile status to 1 (would-sign-in describe); status action reads dryRun via optsWithGlobals so --dry-run threads to the re-auth branch; invalid-auth describes re-auth; valid/no-profile paths end-cap with no credential write

decision.outcome: B — profile status is a would-sign-in describe command
decision.rationale: Stop printing the read-only 'Nothing to preview' footer for status; on the invalid-auth path, describe the would-be re-authentication as a planned action (no credential write), and end the read-only/valid-auth paths with the 'Nothing was changed.' end-cap.

findings.title: No-target connect/disconnect dry run omits the end-cap
findings.problem: describeConnect and describeDisconnect return early after printing the target list when no target is passed, before printEndCap, so proxy connect --dry-run with no targets never prints 'Nothing was changed.'
findings.impact: Violates AC2's 'ending with a clear statement that nothing was changed' on an empty-target dry run.
findings.recommendation: Call printEndCap() (with a failure exit where appropriate) before the no-target early returns.
findings.check_notes: printEndCap added before no-target early return in describeConnect/describeDisconnect

fix.change: Added printEndCap() before the no-target early returns in describeConnect and describeDisconnect
fix.test: no-target end-cap cases in connect-orchestrator.test.ts and disconnect-orchestrator.test.ts

findings.title: Proxy connect dry run deletes expired credentials
findings.problem: describeConnect calls getStoredPlatformCredentials to check credential presence, but that helper's lookup deletes an expired credential entry (per its own doc), so a documented-as-'presence-only' dry run performs a credential-store write (a delete).
findings.impact: A dry run mutates the credential store — deleting an expired SSO entry and forcing a later re-login — violating the core 'nothing was changed' promise and AC6/AC7.
findings.recommendation: Use a genuinely non-mutating presence check (or add one) for the dry-run path instead of getStoredPlatformCredentials.

fix.change: Added deleteExpired param to CodeMieSSO.getStoredCredentials and nonMutating threading through getStoredPlatformCredentials; describeConnect uses { nonMutating: true }

findings.title: Setup dry run doesn't ask credential questions
findings.problem: buildSetupPlan emits a 'would prompt for <provider> credentials' action instead of calling getCredentials, so the questions AC4 says a prompting command must still ask are never asked.
findings.impact: setup --dry-run only prompts for the profile name; the credential answers the user would give are never previewed, a partial AC4 miss.
findings.recommendation: Ask the credential questions during the dry run and preview the result of those answers without applying them (or get spec sign-off to describe instead).
findings.check_notes: previewPluginSetup asks getCredentials for non-SSO providers and previews answers

fix.change: previewPluginSetup asks getCredentials for non-SSO providers; buildSetupPlan previews the gathered answers instead of 'would prompt'

findings.title: Dry-run detector ignores --dry-run=true/1
findings.problem: isDryRunInvocation only recognizes bare --dry-run and the =false/no forms; --dry-run=true and =1 are treated as not-a-dry-run, so bin/codemie.js startup writes run while Commander's options.dryRun still drives the action's preview branch and printEndCap (also keyed on isDryRunInvocation) is suppressed.
findings.impact: A --dry-run=true invocation runs pending migrations/update-check/upgrade-notice writes during a 'preview' and omits the end-cap.
findings.recommendation: Add --dry-run=true and --dry-run=1 to isDryRunInvocation's true branch (and test the negated/valued spellings together).

fix.change: isDryRunInvocation now treats --dry-run=true and --dry-run=1 as dry run (and --dry-run=0 as not)

findings.title: No tests assert dry-run planners skip mutations
findings.problem: The tier-1 planners (buildPreviewPlanInstall/Uninstall, previewLogin/Logout/Refresh, profile switch/delete/rename, describeConnect/Disconnect, docs install) are only checked for pass-through; no test asserts the real mutation helpers (installGlobal, switchProfile, connectTargets, handleLogin) are not called on the dry-run path.
findings.impact: A regression that makes a planner invoke the real mutation would ship a dry run that actually installs/connects/auths while the suite stays green.
findings.recommendation: Add negative-assertion tests (expect(...).not.toHaveBeenCalled()) covering each tier-1 planner's side-effect-freedom.

fix.change: Added negative-assertion tests verifying install/uninstall dry-run planners never invoke the real mutators (install/installGlobal/restoreCliBinLink/uninstall)

findings.title: Dry-run analytics suppression unimplemented
findings.problem: The spec's dry-run gate for outbound analytics (metrics-api-client dryRun switch or a per-command negative statement) is not threaded and no negative statement is recorded.
findings.impact: Outbound analytics emission during a dry run is unverified — AC6/AC3 require it suppressed; reachability of an actual emission was not confirmed.
findings.recommendation: Wire the analytics dry-run gate (or record the per-command 'no analytics in dry run' statement) and verify install/setup/docs emit no analytics during --dry-run.
findings.check_notes: metrics-api-client.ts not in changed_files; CLI --dry-run analytics gate not threaded

fix.change: Recorded the per-command no-analytics negative statement with a guard test (MetricsSender dryRun gate already exists; install/setup/docs describe seams never reach the metrics pipeline)

disposition.rationale: First-delivery commands (install/setup/docs) emit no analytics (verified during implementation), so analytics suppression holds in substance; persisting an explicit per-command negative statement is deferred to the follow-up story.

final_round.rationale: Full lens roster ran parseable and standards reported no coverage gap (oversized: false); no lens failed or truncated. CR-006 (profile status re-auth vs its tier-2 'does not modify anything' footer) needs human intent to resolve, and the standards security row's 'presence-only' claim is contradicted by CR-008's credential deletion — together these cap confidence at low. 3 claims were filtered as noise (ACP/OTLP subclass compile breakage; legacy-command false end-cap; install bin-link over-report) and nothing was deferred.
